title: Scripture and the Church
searchTerms: Word of God and the Church
definition: Scripture and the church belong together because the church is gathered, governed, corrected, and sent under the authority of God's Word.
summary: A healthy church is not built on personality, preference, or performance, but on the apostolic Word, sound doctrine, worship, fellowship, prayer, and mission.
christFocus: Christ rules His church by His Word and shepherds His people through the truth He has given.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Scripture and the Church teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to scripture and the church by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
